result.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
result.summary: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function $ρ$, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant $c$: linear diffusion ($c=-1$, $ω\equiv0$), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap ($c=-1$, $ω\neq0$), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency ($c=+1$). An exact moment identity gives $ρ$ in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is comparative: each family requires a different component of the construction and has a different honest control. In family I, the diffusive-time reparametrisation alone reproduces most of the gain, so that family is a poor test of the idea and shows why an ablation is mandatory. In family II no time reparametrisation exists, the control degrades accuracy, and the amplitude prefactor becomes essential (40.8x). In family III the adiabatic approximation also fails, and the quadratic phase factor is what matters (5.7x). The method does not help when the reduced solution does not converge to a fixed point: its extrapolation advantage then disappears. The reduction itself is the classical scaling-variable change of the self-similar-asymptotics literature; what is new is the moment identity that makes it architectural for time-dependent coefficients, and the comparative anatomy above.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 Ermakov–Pinney 尺度函数 ρ 作为无参数嵌入写入 PINN 输入层，用同一构造覆盖线性扩散、时变陷阱扩散与时变频率量子振子，并借助矩恒等式从初值闭式得到 ρ，进而比较三个问题族各自依赖哪个组件、何种对照才是诚实对照。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「把方程已确定的尺度结构以闭式方式注入网络输入、避免容量浪费」及「必须做消融才能区分真实贡献」的思路，或可类比 LVR 中任务必要信息与各组件贡献分配的问题表述，供核查。
